Today I've got a proposal on how to deal with moderators who delete submissions and comments in default subverses. In this post my goal isn't just to assume worst case scenario, I'd want the situation broken up into sections where we can analyzed what has happened and find a verdict.

Usually when moderators deletes something in a subverse it would be due to a cause. The cause could be broken rules, removal of spam or personal disagreement with something a user has posted. If we analyze what qualifies as a broken rule as an example we would need to firstly read the subverse sidebar where rules would usually be posted. If we look at /v/funny as an example you can see that the sidebar has the usual rules that you'd expect, which is usually tag NSFW stuff and report/downvote spam if you see it. If a post was removed due to spam but wasn't your typical MH101 stuff you should check the user's posts and see how many times they've posted that comment. Atko has said that 20% of the user's comments could be an advertisement. Unless you want to look through a spammers comment history it's better to view their profile and see how many comments they've posted then check their comments tab to determine see if they've broken the 20% rule. If they have the deletion would be justified, else we should begin the question of the moderator.

If a moderator has removed a comment that doesn't break the 20% rule 9/10 times it's not a big deal and if you explain the situation as you interpreted it to the moderator and then pointed out the 20% rule they'd likely be willing to apologize and in some cases remove the post. Just because a moderator removes a comment that isn't spam that doesn't mean you need to verbally abuse them and downvote their comments to a point where they can't downvote themselves and create an atmosphere where they're likely to be locked out of their account. We've seen with @She, @Mathgrunt, @eggnogg and many more moderators that deleting a comment can ruin your CCP and attract harassment.

If you look at @eggnogg as an example you'll see that he deleted only a handful of comments. I'd personally estimate that 1 out of every 1000 comments or submission had been deleted by eggnogg. That still leaves an extremely successful "undeleted" rate which doesn't warrant the brigading and harassment to happen. If 9/10 posts that weren't spam or rule breaking contributions to the Voat community it would be a completely different scenario, probably enough for Atko or Puttitout to act. Even then that doesn't mean you have to resort to brigading or harassment.

The best way to analyze the situation would be to get everyone's view along with sources on what they interpreted and then aggregate it into a single answer of what happened. We can't allow just one side of the story to be heard as well with this solution, there needs to be the moderators story as well and that needs to be considered when making a final answer to moderator abuse.

Thank you for reading my suggestion, please leave any feedback or suggestions below.
